key_insight: Embedding random Fourier features into a PINN reduces spectral bias, enabling much better capture of sharp elastoplastic gradients in non-associative Mohr-Coulomb geomaterials.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a faster, mesh-free surrogate for FEM that can predict displacement, stress, and plastic zone evolution in geotechnical elasto-plastic analysis.
method: Random Fourier feature mapping is added to the PINN input layer to improve representation of high-frequency field variations.
A multi-objective loss enforces equilibrium, constitutive laws, and KKT conditions using FEM guidance.
Strain-adaptive sampling focuses training on regions with steep gradients and plastic localization.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark cases, FF-PINN reduced errors by up to about 66% in displacement and 27% in stress, reproduced plastic zones more faithfully, and converged in roughly half the epochs of a conventional PINN.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful loss balancing and sampling design, and the approach is validated against specific 2D benchmark cases rather than full 3D field problems.
paper_title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model
